items.synopsis: On EX2300 and EX3400 devices, Network Processing Unit telemetry counters can be incorrect after device or PFE bring up
items.description: On Junos EX2300 and EX3400 switches, after the device or the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) starts, some hardware telemetry or statistics related to Network Processing Unit can appear incorrect or fail to report as expected; network traffic is not affected.

items.synopsis: The Lag-link & Aggregate-member-info tags are missing in 'show interfaces fab1 detail | display xml'
items.description: The 'Link:' and 'Aggregate member links:' sections are missing for cli: 'show interfaces fab0.0 detail'and 'show interfaces fab1.0 detail' commands. The affected platforms are Fleming (SRX1600/SRX2300/SRX4120/SRX4300) and Casino Royale (SRX4700).

items.synopsis: HA failover not triggered after PFE process crash in chassis cluster (MNHA) mode on SRX1600/2300/4300/4700
items.description: On SRX1600/2300/4300/4700 platforms configured in chassis cluster (MNHA) mode, when a PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) process crash occurs on the active node, HA failover is not triggered because the failure condition is not detected by the HA subsystem.

items.synopsis: The JSD server fails to start the local SSL certificate for the SSL-based telemetry services in the FIP mode
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when FIPS is enabled, the JSD server fails to start if a local SSL certificate is configured on telemetry; as a result, telemetry services using SSL certificates are unavailable.

items.category: BBE UP Session Manager related issues
items.synopsis: L2TP subscriber session failure in BNG CUPS scenario
items.description: On Junos MX platforms and Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms that support BNG CUPS ( Broadband Network Gateway Control and User Plane Separation), L2TP (Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol) subscriber sessions will fail to come up. When this happens, the subscriber session does not bind correctly and no data traffic will pass for the affected subscribers.

items.synopsis: RPD crashed while stale route LLGR timer expired
items.description: When using BGP-LU with LLGR (Long-Lived Graceful Restart), advertising lo0 addresses as direct peers, while BGP-VPN runs on top of BGP-LU. When the customer shuts down the BGP peer, and the LLGR timer expires, if the RPD tries to bring the connection back up, the RPD process may restart. The issue is due to failing to clean up an unconfigured peer data structure after the LLGR stale timer expires, leaving the peer in the Connect state.

items.synopsis: PIC/LMIC will be stuck in offline state with MACsec
items.description: On MX304 platforms/LC4800/LC4802 linecards, when LMIC(Line Modular Interface Card)/PIC (Peripheral Interface Card ) is restarted on MACsec (Media Access Control Security) enabled interfaces, LMIC/PIC will be stuck in offline state which results into traffic loss.

items.synopsis: IPv4 Family Statistics for subinterfaces streaming as zero
items.description: When the CLI setting "set forwarding-options family inet route-accounting" is enabled to activate IPv4 route accounting statistics, the streaming for /interfaces/interface/subinterfaces/subinterface incorrectly reports all IPv4 counters as zero. This occurs even though IPv4 traffic is successfully forwarded and accounted for in the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) .

items.synopsis: Core is seen in Group based policy configuration with switch-port trunk configuration
Redundant PFE label swap during MHL2circuit failover leading to traffic loss
items.description: On all ACX5448 platform, during a CCC(circuit cross-connect)-to-MPLS primary and protect path next-hop swap event, the in-labels are also being swapped. However, these labels were already swapped during earlier MPLS-to-CCC events. This additional, unintended swap by the PFE leads to traffic disruption.

items.synopsis: cli-pfe does not terminate immediately when user issues Ctrl-C
items.description: A cli-pfe show command may continue to gather data in the background after the user issues a Ctrl-C. Eventually the background command will complete. However, the CPU usage for the cli-pfe process will continue to be high while it is still running.

items.synopsis: Incorrect CCC state displayed when IFL or interface status is absent
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, When the logical interface (IFL) is not present, the system incorrectly reports the Circuit Cross-Connect (CCC) state as CCC Up. Similarly, when the interface status itself is not available, the pseudowire state is shown as CCC_Up or CCC_Down. The pseudowire state should instead be reported as Not Applicable, since the underlying interface or IFL required to determine a valid CCC state does not exist. Displaying CCC Up/Down incorrectly in the absence of interface.

items.synopsis: ARP resolution failure for /32 static host routes via IRB in EVPN virtual-switch routing instances
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms that support EVPN (Ethernet VPN) virtual-switch routing instances, ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) resolution fails for static host routes configured with a /32 mask when the next-hop interface is an IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) interface and the destination host resides in a different subnet. As a result, ARP entries are not installed, MAC (Media Access Control) addresses of destination hosts are not learned, and traffic destined to those hosts becomes unreachable, causing service impact.

items.synopsis: Interfaces down after Virtual Chassis reboot
items.description: On all Junos EX Series platforms, following a Virtual Chassis (VC) reboot, random interface links GE(Gigabit) and XE(10 Gigabit) intermittently appear in a down state at the Interface Descriptor (IFD) level, even though the physical link remains operational.

items.synopsis: NDPv6 policer violations are not being triggered while ARP violations are unexpectedly logged
items.description: On all EX platforms, even though the NDPv6 (Neighbor Discovery Protocol for IPv6) policer threshold is exceeded, no NDPv6 violations are recorded. Instead, the system reports ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) violations, which is unexpected since the traffic being sent consists solely of IPv6 RA (Router Advertisement) packets.

items.synopsis: On Junos devices supporting subscriber services acting as DHCPv6 relay randomly deletes IA_NA or IA_PD binding/route
items.description: On all Junos devices supporting subscriber services, in case of dual stack DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) subscribers with IA_NA (Identity Association for Non-temporary Address) and IA_PD (Identity Association for Prefix Delegation) bindings with lease times (For the assignment of IPv6 address to a client device), when a client initiates separate renew exchanges for the IA_NA and IA_PD, and once client and DHCP server are in sync with these timers, there can be a race condition at Junos device which is DHCPv6 relay, has not refreshed lease timer and can go out of sync. This can result in deleting IA_NA/IA_PD binding and route to get deleted for that subscriber only. This causes one of the leg for IA_PD or IA_NA to go down for that subscriber, which can result in traffic impact for that leg.

items.synopsis: When Macsec is enabled on 1G interface, Auto-neg needs to be disabled for MX301.
items.description: When Macsec is enabled on 1G interface, Auto-neg needs to be disabled for MX301. Config to disable auto-negotiation: set interfaces <1g-intf-name> gigether-options no-auto-negotiation

items.synopsis: Unable to create large number of ifls on 1G interface
items.description: On Junos MX301 and MX304 platforms there is a scaling issue to configure more than 1024 ifls (logical interfaces) on 1-Gigabit ethernet interfaces. Further interfaces will not work. There is no impact on the existing interfaces and system works fine with 1024 logical interfaces.

items.synopsis: Truncated log messages are seen for sensor logs on MX301 and SRX4700 platforms
items.description: On Junos MX301 and SRX4700 platforms, there is the change in log message for the CB 0_TEMP_0 sensor. This is a display issue with no functional impact.

items.synopsis: The license add using 'terminal' option fails in a controller setup
items.description: On Junos MX304 and MX10K platforms, the 'terminal' option is not supported in controller satellite setup along with device-list option since terminal is local to controller and cannot be used to install license in satellite. The user can use the 'file' option and the file needs to be copied to the device and later user can use the same command with the file option to add the license.

items.synopsis: NGPE COS: Adjustment for 54B VXLAN header for traffic going from NGPE AD to SD
items.description: 54B VXLAN header will not be accounted during COS shaping on NGPE EP port for packets going from AD to SD.

items.category: Category for all Infrastructure & PFE related issues support for NGPE
items.synopsis: The connectivity to Satellite devices will be lost if MTU on NGPE EP is set to greater than 1522
items.description: In fusion setup on MX platforms, in a NGPE(next-gen port-extender) topology, If the MTU on an NGPE EP is set to more than 1522, and there are host bound packets of size are than 1522, this will cause the PFE crash. This will cause the system to go down as the connectivity to SD will be lost.

items.category: JUNOS Network App Infrastructure (for ping, traceroute, etc)
items.synopsis: Fetch command output format changed and completion percentage not displayed
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, the output format of the fetch command changed after upgrading to a newer upstream version of the utility. The earlier format displayed an explicit completion indicator (for example, 100%). The upgraded version removed this indicator.

items.category: vpls on branch (jseries and srx) platforms
items.synopsis: ISIS adjacency not coming up on SRX 3XX series platforms in VPLS topology
items.description: On SRX 3XX platforms, due to incorrect mbuf (Memory Buffer) allocation, the ISIS (Intermediate System-to-Intermediate System) packets with MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) tag transiting over a L2VPN (Layer 2 Virtual Private Network) are dropped if the packet size exceeds 1500 bytes resulting in the ISIS adjacency remaining stuck in the initializing state, leading to routing issues. This issue is intermittent and observed only when the SRX 3XX device is serving as the PE in MPLS L2VPN network.

items.synopsis: The dcpfe process crashes when adding or removing classifier configuration on QFX5210
items.description: On QFX5210 platform with Class of Service (CoS), the dcpfe process crashes when classifier is configured or removed on interface with active traffic. This can affect traffic forwarding till dcpfe process restarts post crash.

items.synopsis: 24.4R2-S1:JUNOS:MACSEC: When connectivity-association properties mka eapol-address is set to unicast address, then MKA session stays in in-progress
items.description: When AE interface (member links) are configured with MACsec, the MKA session establishes successfully when the default standard MAC address is used. However, when a custom unicast MAC address is configured, the MKA session does not come up. This is not a common use case, but the workaround is to allow the MKA session to operate with the default MAC address instead of a custom unicast MAC address.

items.category: Trio pfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: VTEP fragmenting VXLAN packets which gets routed into IRB or any L3 interface as underlay over VXLAN tunnels
items.description: On all Junos MX platforms, in VXLAN (Virtual Extensible Local Area Network) tunnel setup, where packets getting routed into an underlay IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) or any L3 interface over VXLAN tunnels, if VTEP (Virtual Tunnel Endpoint) receiving an IPv4 packet with its total packet size bigger than the outgoing IRB/L3 interface IFL (Interface Logical) MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) then VTEP fragments outer IPv4 packet and each fragment is sent to the remote VTEP which eventually drops them causing packet drop.

items.synopsis: Slow memory leak triggered by subscribing to the pipeline sensor for a long duration
items.description: On Junos platforms with MPC 1-9, LC2101, LC480, LC2103 line-cards and MX204, a slow memory is observed when subscribing to the pipeline sensor ( path is /components/component/integrated-circuit/pipeline-counters/). Over time, this causes a gradual increase in heap memory usage. Increase in heap memory usage beyond a certain threshold will lead to FPC crash resulting in loss of services and traffic over that FPC.

items.synopsis: JDI-RCT:M/Mx: : NGMVPN multicast traffic gets dropped post Change route-distinguisher/route-target on L3VPN instances.
items.description: Not consistent issue and happens when RD and RT change is done in all routing instances while the traffic is running. Also sometimes issue seen only in certain instances. When issue happens there will be traffic drop for inclusive tunnel and affecting all flows on inclusive tunnel and it may not recover unless some external events like route change occurs.

items.synopsis: On MX301 rpd may core when logical-systems configuration is used to create EVPN-VPWS
items.description: On MX301 rpd may core when logical-systems configuration is used to create EVPN-VPWS

items.synopsis: zeroize command not working
items.description: zeroize command not working

items.synopsis: VRRP traffic dropped after priority change due to pinned MAC entry on peer device
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) priority is changed, the VRRP virtual Media Access Control (MAC) address can remain pinned as a static entry on the remote device. As a result, MAC movement does not occur correctly, and VRRP packets are dropped on the leaf device. This impacts VRRP operation after priority changes.

items.synopsis: MX10008 PTP IRB: Spike seen during noise generation test with 255 master scaled stream with 2 IRB interface
items.description: During noise generation tests on MX10008 and MX10004 platforms with LC480 line cards, a spike could occasionally be observed in T1/T4 TE measurements when PTP master streams are scaled to 255 with G.8275.2 over IRB is configured. This spike occurs approximately every 10, 000 seconds and is typically seen when the number of master PTP streams exceeds 128. Additionally, there is a configurable limit on the pps rate for Sync and Delay packets (upto 64pps), and exceeding the recommended threshold may contribute to this behavior.

items.synopsis: Transient Traffic Duplication During EVPN Multihomed Spine Reboot in Collapsed EVPN-VXLAN Deployments
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms with EVPN-VxLAN Multihoming scenario, in EVPN multihomed (ESI) deployments without core isolation, a temporary traffic duplication could occur during a spine reboot or any event that forces forwarding re-convergence.

items.description: In EX4400 devices with 4x25G or 1x100g ULM, when we perform PIC online, CPU hog by CMQFX thread may be seen for as much as 3.5seconds

items.description: EX4400-48F: When we have SFP-SX optics plugged in EX4400-48F device in the ports 0 to 35 and it is rebooted, the activity LED remains on.

items.synopsis: [RLI-59204:Model-X:MX301:HTTP/1.1 307 redirect responses are missing from the IPv6 packet captures]

items.synopsis: MACsec traffic encryption failure after SFP OIR with interface and session up
items.description: On MX301 and platforms with PTX10K-LC1301-36QD, After SFP (Small Form-factor Pluggable transceiver) Online Insertion and Removal (OIR) on a MACsec (Media Access Control Security) enabled interface, the link and MACsec session remain UP, but MACsec encryption and decryption stop functioning. This results in traffic loss and causes service impact.

items.synopsis: CLI based Virtium SSD firmware upgrade is missing
items.description: Support for Virtium SSD firmware upgrade for Mclaren RCB not available in 25.2R1-S1. Fixed in later releases.

items.synopsis: Suppress humidity sensor CLI command and corresponding code in McLaren MX
items.description: Humidity Sensor CLI command is not applicable in McLaren RCB. The command has been suppressed in later releases

items.synopsis: POL current/power values in CLI may not match actual readings
items.description: On McLaren RCB, display-only issue in Junos CLI show chassis environment : current/power for some of the POLs are shown as 0, observed in 25.2R1-S1. Fixed in later releases.

items.description: [MX301]: Carrier transition count show 2 for ae interface instead of 1

items.description: JDI-RCT:M/Mx: ISIS session over MPC11 cards flapped due to "3-Way handshake failed" during ISSU (FRU upgrade stage - reboot phase)

items.description: On MX301, rpd core may be seen after deactivate/activate protocol isis trigger

items.synopsis: The rpd process crash is observed after a graceful restart in the RSVP-TE scenario
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms with Graceful Restart and RSVP-TE (Resource Reservation Protocol - Traffic Engineering) configured, an rpd crash is observed, leading to traffic impact after a Graceful Restart if a PVC (Permanent Virtual Circuit) fails to allocate correctly during this recovery process, leaving it in an incomplete or unallocated state, and the system attempts to clean up or remove this unallocated PVC.

items.synopsis: JDI-RCT:M/Mx: during ISSU , may observe some traffic drops for L3VPN streams during FRU upgrade stage (HW resync phase).
items.description: On MX platforms, during ISSU, some traffic drop may occur in HW sync phase for few L3VPN flows. The traffic recovers post HW sync phase. This issue is not specific to 25.4R1.

items.synopsis: Significant multicast traffic loss observed during ISSU in NextGeneration MVPN (NGMVPN) deployments
items.description: On MX480 platforms running Junos OS, multicast traffic loss can occur during InService Software Upgrade (ISSU) in NGMVPN deployments using both IPMSI and SPMSI with a nonzero threshold, as FPCs upgrade and synchronize and multicast statistics may briefly report zero, triggering SPMSI withdrawal and fallback to IPMSI, which may not yet be fully programmed, leading to temporary loss of only SPMSI flows for a variable duration (~180230 seconds) while IPMSI flows continue normally; the issue can affect both IPv4 and IPv6 multicast.

items.synopsis: A vmcore may be observed on the backup when there are changes to configuration attributes related to EP IFDs are performed with GRES configured.
items.description: A vmcore may be observed on the backup when any of the following configurations are performed on the EP IFDs with GRES configured 1. Port Speed change on the EP IFDs When configuring(set)/unconfiguring(delete) port speed on the EP IFDs using the config stanza "chassis port-extender fpc-slot <> pic-slot <> port <> speed <>" 2. Changing the configuration attribute "cascade-port"/"target-mode"/"device" under the config hierarchy "chassis port-extender fpc-slot <>" "chassis port-extender fpc-slot <> cascade-port <>" "chassis port-extender fpc-slot <> target-mode <> " "chassis port-extender fpc-slot <> device <>" Impact: 1. Traffic will be impacted. 2. Backup RE is not available for graceful switchover until state resync/replay completes from the master. Though vmcore is observed, backup does not reboot as it is system generated live core for debugging.

items.synopsis: High CPU utilization of the acx-arm-feb process after upgrade or reboot when PTP or SyncE is configured
items.description: On ACX710 platforms running Junos OS, the acx-arm-feb process can reach 100 percent CPU utilization after an upgrade or reboot when PTP or SyncE is configured and the associated interfaces are enabled. This condition may result in degraded operational responsiveness and partial traffic impact.

items.synopsis: On MX301, IGMP may not get enabled by default when PIM is enabled
items.description: On MX301, IGMP may not get enabled by default when PIM is enabled. Use "set protocols igmp interface" to explicitly enable IGMP

As a result, service impact happened till all FPCs become online.

items.description: In all Junos MX platforms acting as the AD (Aggregation Device) in a Junos Fusion deployment, a Junos software upgrade causes the smdp (Satellite Platform and Management Daemon) process to crash impacting forwarding plane services. This issue is observed when AD nodes are moved to a higher Junos version while the SD (Satellite nodes) are still running a lower version.
